findings.claim: NO single shared mechanism can faithfully close a large class. Largest repeated class: 216 TagResource/UntagResource/ListTagsForResource stubs in 84 crates (plus 26 resource-policy stubs in 12 crates, 2873 Describe/Get/List stubs in 215 crates), but AWS tagging semantics are service-specific: 204 vs 200 success (Image Builder, Aurora DSQL), Content-Length on an empty 204 (MediaPackage), 404 ResourceNotFoundException vs 403 (Chatbot), reserved 'aws:' message, ARN grammars/limits, IAM gates, tag-on-create propagation, cross-service visibility. No shared tag code exists in vendor/ (exhaustive rg); only 25 crates have their own state/{tagging,tags}.rs. The central Resource Groups Tagging API is a VIEW over 13 owners needing one Cargo dependency + one arm of visit() + one of tagged_resources() per owner. Codegen (build-support/src/lib.rs:554-630) emits only wiring. The only shared mechanism today is the 501 channel itself, which keeps the class uniformly unimplemented.
findings.root_cause: InMemoryEngine is a TypeId -> per-service state type-map (vendor/engine/src/lib.rs:103-118); the framework knows no resource identity, success status or refusal. findings.root_cause: A success with no backing state is indistinguishable from a real implementation to a client asserting only that the call succeeded; the marker is the machine-readable census.
